template: You are on the Grafana dashboard '{{v1}}' (URL {{v4}}). Do two things and save them persistently: (1) Add the tag 'bench' to the dashboard — enter dashboard edit mode, open the dashboard settings (gear icon) > General, and add the tag 'bench' in the tags field, then Save. (2) Set the dashboard's time range to the last 6 hours — open the time picker in the top bar and choose 'Last 6 hours'. Then, IMPORTANT: save the dashboard in a way that persists the time range into the saved dashboard — in the save dialog, tick the 'Update default time range' checkbox before clicking Save, so the 6-hour range is stored as the dashboard's default. Verify afterwards: reload the dashboard page fresh and confirm the tag 'bench' appears (e.g. in dashboard settings > General tags field, or in the dashboard list/search result for this dashboard) and the time picker shows 'Last 6 hours' right after a fresh reload. Report exactly what you observed for the tag and the time range after the reload.

reportTemplate.summary: Both changes are saved persistently on '{{v1}}' (uid {{v5}}). Tag 'bench' was added via Edit > Settings > General > Tags, and the time range was set to Last 6 hours and stored as the dashboard default by ticking 'Update default time range' before SAVE (confirmed by the 'Dashboard saved' message). After fresh, parameter-less reloads of {{v4}}: the breadcrumb reads '{{v1}}', the time picker reads 'Last 6 hours', Settings > General shows the 'bench' tag, and the stored JSON model contains "tags": ["bench"] and "time": {"from": "now-6h", "to": "now"}. Both panels persist too ('{{v2}} Notes' with 'Notes for run {{v2}}', and '{{v2}} Availability' Stat = 17.8).
